headline: Approved a $100,000 transfer from the commercial loan account to cover operating costs, and a Visitor Center lease by 3-1 vote.
summary: A $100,000 transfer from the commercial loan account was approved to cover operating costs, to be replenished later. A Visitor Center lease passed 3-1, and exploratory planning for a soup kitchen at 69 Exchange Street was approved. Discussion also covered cash flow problems and mold repairs at 25 Mendon Street.
decisions: Approved use of 354 Pine Street for the Guatemalan Festival on September 12, 2026, subject to insurance and deposit, 4-0.
Approved transfer of $100,000 from the commercial loan account to cover operating expenses, to be replenished when funds are received, 5-0.
Approved the Commercial Loans Delinquency Policy as amended to require board notice of delinquencies at the next meeting, 5-0.
Approved the Visitor Center lease, subject to the landlord voiding the outstanding holdover invoice, 3-1, with the Chair opposed.
Authorized staff to begin exploratory planning for a soup kitchen at 69 Exchange Street, including space assessment, layout, and cost evaluation, 4-0.

plain_text:
Pawtucket Redevelopment Agency 
Meeting Minutes 
August 4, 2026, 12:15 PM 
 
Call to Order  
The meeting was called to order at 12:15 p.m. 
 
Roll Call  
A quorum was established. In attendance:  Larry Monastesse, Brian Murtha, Tim O’Riley, 
Mark McLaughlin (Ineida Anderson Rocha arrived at 12:25 p.m.) 
 
Others:  Jason Pezzullo, Tim Chapman, Michael Cassidy, Mary Bourdeau, Mark Goudreau, 
Irene Santos, Olivia Joseph, Samuel Joseph, Peggy Martinez, Cindy Miranda, Henry 
Vasquez, Exneider Vasquez, Sandra Cano, Irina Batyuk, Mark Hayward 
  
Public Input Session - None 
 
Minutes of Previous Meeting – June 30, 2026  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the minutes of June 30, 2026, seconded by Mr. 
O’Riley.  Motion carried 4-0. 
 
Consent Agenda  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the consent agenda, seconded by Mr. O’Riley.  Motion 
carried 4-0. 
 
Commercial Loan Report 
RI Spirit – It was reported that the borrower had paid off a lien on a separate property. 
However, the PRA's own loan to RI Spirit remains in active litigation.  It was  indicated the 
matter is on hold pending resolution among multiple parties involved in the litigation, with a 
receiver not yet having been appointed.  
 
Village Restaurant – It was reported there is no new update, noting it remains an ongoing 
matter to be monitored. 
 
Black Market Realty – It was noted that the matter is in legal proceedings, with no further 
information available at this time. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the commercial loan report, seconded by Mr. O’Riley.  
Motion carried 4-0. 
 
 
New Business 
Request for 354 Pine Street – Guatemalan Festival September 12, 2026  
Ms. Martinez was in attendance to request the use of 354 Pine Street for the Guatemalan 
Festival on September 12, 2026. It was confirmed that a PRA insurance policy is already in 
place covering the site, and that the organization has used the property for similar events in 
the past. The board discussed the standard deposit process, whereby a $1,000 check is held 
prior to the event, the site is inspected afterward, and the check is returned upon satisfactory 
cleanup. Staff noted there may be some active environmental work occurring at the far end of
the property and committed to inspecting the site to confirm whether that area is closed off or 
sufficiently separated from the event footprint, and to coordinate with Chris Crawley if 
necessary. Members were satisfied that the standard process would address cleanup concerns. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the request for the use of 354 Pine Street for the 
Guatemalan Festival on September 12, 2026 subject to insurance and deposit, seconded by 
Mr. McLaughlin.  Motion carried 4-0.  
 
Ineida Anderson Rocha arrived at 12:25 p.m. 
 
PRA Financial Information and Budget Update  
Ms. Batyuk presented a financial update reflecting the PRA's ongoing cash flow challenges. 
A reimbursement had recently been received from US Bank for utility expenses, which was 
applied to outstanding invoices. Several new commercial loans remain pending. Black 
Market Realty continues to be in legal proceedings with no payments received. The audit for 
the prior fiscal year has not yet been finalized. 
 
Mr. Pezzullo reported that he has been engaged in ongoing conversations with the city 
administration regarding the need for a cash infusion to sustain PRA operations, emphasizing 
that the PRA does not have sufficient revenue streams to independently fund its operating 
costs. He indicated that the city is aware of the situation and that further news is expected 
soon, though no formal commitment has been received. 
 
Ms. Santos proposed, as an interim stopgap measure, transferring $100,000 from the PRA's 
commercial loan account—which holds a balance of approximately $333,000, largely 
representing Women's Development Corporation funds—to cover outstanding operating 
expenses such as insurance, utilities, and vendor invoices. It was clarified that these funds are 
not tied to any federal grant program such as CDBG, making the transfer permissible. The 
board discussed the importance of maintaining a paper trail and ensuring that the funds would 
be replenished, whether through US Bank reimbursements, city appropriation, or other 
funding sources. Members acknowledged the risk that drawing from the commercial loan 
account reduces capital available for new loans, but agreed the measure was necessary to 
keep operations functioning. It was noted that a meaningful portion of the outstanding bills—
approximately 70 percent—may qualify for US Bank reimbursement. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the transfer of $100,000 from the commercial loan 
account to cover operating expenses, with the condition that the funds be replenished when 
received from US Bank reimbursements, city appropriation, grant, or other funding, was 
made and seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
CRMC Approval – Fish Ladders  
Mr. Cassidy reported that the Coastal Resources Management Council (CRMC) has reviewed 
and approved the fish ladder project as proposed, with no objections. The required 
documentation has been recorded. The PRA's involvement to date has been limited to 
facilitating the permit submission process. Mr. Cassidy clarified that the PRA has made no 
agreements to sell or donate land in connection with this project. Any future progress would 
require the project proponents to secure funding—estimated at approximately $10,000,000—
and to negotiate easements on the Apex and Broadway properties with the PRA's approval.
The PRA retains ownership of the relevant land. No vote was required; this was presented as 
an informational update. 
 
 
Municap Invoice No. 062026-408, dated 6/26/26 - $456.25  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve Municap Invoice No. 062026-408, dated June 26, 
2026, in the amount of $456.25 seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Municap Invoice No. 062026-026, dated 6/26/26 - $1,137.50  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve Municap Invoice No. 062026-026, dated June 26, 
2026, in the amount of $1,137.50 seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha.  The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Municap Invoice No. 072026-395, dated 7/28/26 - $787.50  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve Municap Invoice No. 072026-395, dated July 28, 
2026, in the amount of $787.50 seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Pare Invoice No. 42, dated 7/27/26 - $10,237.50  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve Pare Invoice No. 42, dated July 27, 2026, in the 
amount of $10,237.50 seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Old Business 
Commercial Loans Delinquency Policy Draft  
The Board reviewed the draft Commercial Loans Delinquency Policy. It was suggested that 
item number one be amended to include a provision requiring staff to notify the PRA board 
of any delinquency at the next scheduled meeting. The Board also discussed the timeframe 
for initial borrower notification, debating whether 31 days or a shorter 15-day window would 
be more appropriate. Mr. Goudreau noted that given current staffing levels, the 31-day 
timeframe was workable, and that the late fee accrues regardless of the notification timing. 
The amendment to notify the board was accepted, and the policy was approved as amended. 
 
Mr. McLaughlin made a motion to approve the Commercial Loans Delinquency Policy Draft, 
as amended to include board notification at the next meeting upon a borrower becoming 
delinquent, was made seconded by Mr. Murtha. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Visitor Center Lease  
The board engaged in an extended discussion regarding the renewal of the lease for the 
Visitor Center space. Staff reported that negotiations with the landlord had been finalized and 
the current draft lease was before the board for approval. The estimated annual cost of the 
lease is approximately $56,400, comprising $1,000 per month in base rent and approximately 
$3,700 per month in the PRA's proportional share (15.27%) of common area operating 
expenses covering a space of approximately 7,675 square feet. The city has budgeted $35,000 
for this purpose, leaving a gap of approximately $21,000 for the current year. In addition, 
approximately $12,000 in costs from the prior fiscal year remain unreimbursed, bringing the 
total shortfall to approximately $33,000. 
 
Members expressed frustration that lease negotiations had not begun earlier in the year, given 
that the situation had been foreseeable since at least March or April. The Chair stated strong 
dissatisfaction with the manner in which the matter had been handled and expressed
reluctance to support the lease given the absence of any written commitment from the city to 
fund the full amount. 
 
Mr. Pezzullo and Mr. Cassidy  provided background context: the PRA had historically 
operated the Visitor Center as part of its portfolio when its accounts were integrated with the 
city. Following the separation of PRA's banking from the city, the funding mechanism broke 
down, leaving the PRA responsible for lease costs without a reliable revenue source to cover 
them. The city continues to expect the PRA to serve as the tenant and operator of the space, 
which is also used as a polling location and for various city activities, staffed by the 
Blackstone Valley Tourism Council. 
 
It was noted a discrepancy between the lease's stated 11 parking spaces and the diagram, 
which reflected only 10, and recommended this be clarified with the landlord. Members also 
discussed the potential for variable costs under Exhibit C of the lease, noting that operating 
expense reconciliations occur annually and that the current year's figures had been provided 
by the landlord in a prior calculation. 
 
Mr. Hayward confirmed that the $35,000 appropriated in the city budget would be transferred 
to the PRA promptly upon execution of the lease, and committed to recommending that the 
full $56,400, as well as any prior-year shortfall, be addressed in the next budget cycle. 
 
The Board discussed and confirmed that the landlord had agreed to void the outstanding 
holdover invoice (approximately $10,000) in exchange for execution of the new lease. It was 
agreed that the lease would be executed and the holdover invoice voided, with the 
understanding that the city would be expected to fund the full annual lease cost. The 
condition regarding city reimbursement was understood to be an internal PRA expectation 
rather than a condition binding on the landlord. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to approve the Visitor Center Lease, subject to the landlord 
voiding the outstanding holdover invoice, was made, seconded by Mr. O’Riley. The motion 
carried 3-1, with the Chair voting in opposition. 
 
Soup Kitchen – Use of 69 Exchange Street  
Mr. Monastesse, Chair, recused himself from this agenda item due to his membership on the 
board of directors of the soup kitchen. The Mr. Murtha, Vice Chair, presided. 
 
Mr. Goudreau reported that the Pawtucket Soup Kitchen is being required to vacate its 
current location as a result of a decision by the Diocese and has been exploring alternative 
spaces. The PRA owns 69 Exchange Street, a building purchased with non-federal funds that 
must be used for services to the city's population, making a soup kitchen use an eligible and 
appropriate purpose. Staff, together with a consultant, recently visited and measured the 
space. A preliminary layout assessment is underway to determine how the soup kitchen's 
operations could be accommodated within the building, including equipment needs and any 
required build-out. Parking was identified as a potential concern to be addressed. 
Staff noted that while CDBG funds cannot be applied to rent, a soup kitchen build-out would 
constitute an eligible CDBG activity, and that there are modest dollars available under the 
city facility improvements category that may be applicable. No financial commitments were 
made at this stage; the board's authorization was sought to proceed with exploratory planning 
and cost assessment.
Mr. McLaughlin made a motion to authorize staff to proceed with exploratory planning for 
the use of 69 Exchange Street by the soup kitchen, including space assessment, layout, and 
cost evaluation, seconded by Ms. Anderson Rocha. The motion carried 4-0. 
 
The Chair returned to preside. 
 
25 Mendon Street Update  
Mr. Goudreau reported that architectural design work for 25 Mendon Street is progressing, 
with the architect continuing to refine the proposed design in consultation with the intended 
tenants. An emergency roof repair cost of $7,500 was completed to address active leaks that 
have been present since the building was acquired. However, the temporary patch work did 
not prevent interior mold from developing during the warm weather months. Staff is in the 
process of obtaining bids for interior demolition and mold remediation, with at least two 
additional quotes required. Mr. O’Riley suggested that an insurance claim be filed, which Mr. 
Goudreau acknowledged had not yet been done but would be pursued. Funding for these 
costs is drawn from a designated fund derived from a prior court judgment related to 258 Pine 
Street. 
 
Executive Session  
Mr. Murtha made a motion to enter Executive Session pursuant to RIGL 42-46-5(a)(2), 
sessions pertaining to collective bargaining or litigation — Item A: Las Delicias Request — 
and pursuant to RIGL 42-46-5(a)(7), a matter related to the investment of public funds where 
premature disclosure would adversely affect the public interest — Item A: Downtown 
Gateway Update — seconded by Mr. O’Riley. The motion carried 5-0. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to seal the minutes of the executive session, seconded by Mr. 
McLaughlin.  Motion carried 5-0. 
 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to return to Open Session, seconded by Mr. McLaughlin.  Motion 
carried 5-0. 
 
 
Upon returning to open session, it was reported that no votes were taken during Executive 
Session. 
 
Adjournment 
Mr. Murtha made a motion to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Mr. McLaughlin. The motion 
carried 5-0.
